title: Everything Matters Equally
coreMove: Break task democracy by ranking work according to leverage, not neatness, urgency, or volume.
sourcePressure: Part 1 begins by dismantling the lie that everything matters equally and pushes the reader from task democracy toward sharper ranking.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Repeating the 80/20 idea as a slogan without forcing a hard ranking.

hook: A single choice changes the whole day
The real priority is hiding under the busy work
Everything Matters Equally as a generic focus opener
counterintuition: Focus is harder than it looks
tryThisNow: Set a timer and list priorities
Write down your one thing without a concrete context
examples: generic office worker choosing email or strategy

exampleSpecs.domain: airport gate operations during a snow delay
exampleSpecs.stakes: one wrong sequencing call strands a crew overnight
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she stops answering every passenger question and ranks crew reassignment above snack vouchers and signage
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a gate podium screen blinking crew timeout in red

exampleSpecs.stakes: three urgent patient callbacks are buried under routine forms
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he moves the callback list above insurance scans after seeing which tasks alter care today
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a fax tray split into routine forms and three highlighted callback slips

exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she ranks generator fuel above folding cots because refrigeration protects insulin and infant formula first
exampleSpecs.firstImage: yellow fuel cans lined beside a taped shelter floor plan

exampleSpecs.domain: jewelry studio before a trade show
exampleSpecs.stakes: one wholesale buyer decides the season's cash flow
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she leaves the display labels unfinished and repairs the clasp on the necklace the buyer requested by name
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a tiny broken clasp under a magnifying lamp beside unprinted labels

exampleSpecs.stakes: missing preliminary figure will kill the proposal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lab sees that polished bios mattered less than one messy-but-real figure showing the effect
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a blotchy preliminary figure taped over a pile of polished bios

exampleSpecs.stakes: morning service depends on one switch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he predicts ballast cleanup can wait, then proves the jammed switch is the item that decides whether trains move
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a headlamp beam fixed on a frozen rail switch at 2:10 a.m.

skillTargets: rank by consequence instead of volume
identify the task that changes the field

tryThisNowSpec: Take today's task list and mark the one item that makes the largest consequence move, even if it is not the easiest to finish.
